desc: Implement a Fenwick tree with `add(i, delta)`, prefix `sum(i)`, and `kth(k)` (find smallest index with prefix sum ≥ k) via binary lifting in O(log N).
Read N and the array P from stdin; initialize the BIT with all N slots free (build in O(N) via bit[i] = i & (-i)).
Loop i from N down to 1: locate slot = BIT.kth(P_i), set answer[slot] = i, and BIT.add(slot, -1).
Justify correctness briefly in comments: when processing i, all elements j > i are already fixed in their final positions, and i must occupy the P_i-th remaining free position.
Write the final answer array to stdout space-separated; verify against the two samples mentally (P = 1 1 2 1 → 4 2 3 1; P = 1 2 3 4 5 → identity).
Confirm complexity O(N log N) and memory O(N), safe for N = 5×10⁵ in Python (use sys.stdin.buffer fast I/O).
